story.title: Modi Announces Free Coaching and AI Training for Youth Following Protests
story.summary: On India's Independence Day, Prime Minister Modi announced a new initiative to provide free online coaching for competitive exams and AI training for 10 million youths. This announcement comes in the wake of significant youth-led protests over alleged exam paper leaks and recruitment irregularities, which also led to the resignation of the education minister. The initiative aims to alleviate the financial burden on families seeking educational support.

related_stories.title: Former Cambridge Professor Jason Arday Found Dead Amid Plagiarism Controversy
related_stories.summary: Jason Arday, the youngest Black professor at the University of Cambridge, was found dead at his home in London. His death occurred one week after he resigned amid allegations of plagiarism. British Prime Minister Andy Burnham described the incident as a 'tragedy on so many levels' and called for reflection on the circumstances surrounding Arday's life and career.

related_stories.title: Trump Seeks Supreme Court Approval for White House Ballroom Construction
related_stories.summary: The Trump administration has requested the U.S. Supreme Court to allow the continuation of construction for a new 90,000-square-foot ballroom at the White House, which is estimated to cost $400 million. This request follows a ruling from an appeals court stating that the project did not have the necessary congressional approval. Administration officials argue that the ballroom is a security necessity and that the project is 'beyond the point of no return.'

related_stories.title: Zambia Resumes Vote Counting After Violence Disruption
related_stories.summary: Zambia has resumed counting votes after a nationwide suspension due to violence that disrupted the election process. The Electoral Commission reported that security threats have been contained following incidents that included the theft of marked ballot papers. Official presidential results are anticipated soon, with authorities urging calm as the counting continues.
